text: Mastering Self is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located behind Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles between Bozé and Cross anytime.

Melon Oil are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from green Ciniculas, or for 114 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in all Arts: Recover HP augments.

The Master Milsaadi (Japanese: , Masutā Mirusādo) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Milsaadi Ganglion, and he must be defeated within three minutes at level 40 at the Jair Fortress in Oblivia during Slovity's Revenge.
Mephite A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a green mephite variant. It can be obtained from Gerhardt, the Lone and Proud in Noctilum.
Mephite B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black mephite variant. It can be obtained from Ferdinand, the Fortuitous in Oblivia.
Mephite C is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a golden mephite variant. It can be obtained from Lask, the Unscrupulous in Sylvalum.
Memento is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Tatsu wearing his father's glasses. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Ties That Bind.

Mechanoids (Japanese: , Mashīn) are a category of enemy in . It includes all enemies of a mechanical or artificial nature. They are commonly built or used by the Ganglion and other antagonists. However a select few are Miran endemic autonomous crafts, constructed from some kind of living metal, or Human-made machines. Human NPCs fought on missions are also considered Mechanoids, as they are later revealed to be mimeosomes. Some common Mechanoids are adversely affected by weather. During electromagnetic storms, energy mist, or rising energy mist weather, these Mechanoids cannot detect by sound. Nevertheless, the Miran Mechanoids (Fal-swos, Oc-servs, and Xe-doms) are unaffected. All Mechanoids
Melee Accuracy Drive is a ground armor Skell Augment in and that increases the Melee Accuracy of the party member's Skell. Its effect caps at 100%.
Melee Attack Drive is a ground armor Skell Augment in and that increases the melee attack of the party member's Skell from 1% to 20%. Its effect caps at 100%.
Melee Accuracy Up is a ground weapon stat augment in and . It increases melee accuracy by 10 to 50. The Skell equivalent is SpecUp.M-ACC.
Melee Attack Up is a ground weapon stat Augment in and that increases melee attack. The Skell equivalent is SpecUp.M-ATK.
Melee Accuracy Boost is a ground weapon stat Augment in and that increases melee attack by a percentage. The Skell equivalent is Boost.M-ACC.
Melee Attack Boost is a ground weapon stat Augment in and that increases melee attack by a percentage. The Skell equivalent is Boost.M-ATK.
Melee: TP Gain Up is a ground weapon mod Augment in and that increases TP gain on melee auto-attacks. The Skell equivalent is Custom.WP-M-GP.
Mechanoid Criticals Up is a ground weapon critical Augment in and that increases critical chance when attacking Mechanoid-classified enemies. The Skell equivalent is CriticalUp.MECHANOID.
Melee: Blackout is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Blackout Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.BLACKOUT.
Melee: Fatigue is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Fatigue Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.FATIGUE.

Melee: Physical Res Down is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Physical Res Down Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.PHYS-DOWN.

Melee: Beam Res Down is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Beam Res Down Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.BEAM-DOWN.

Melee: Ether Res Down is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Ether Res Down Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.ETHER-DOWN.

Melee: Thermal Res Down is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Thermal Res Down Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.THERM-DOWN.

Melee: Electric Res Down is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Electric Res Down Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.ELEC-DOWN.

Melee: Gravity Res Down is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Gravity Res Down Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.GRAV-DOWN.
Melee: Blaze is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Blaze Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.BLAZE.
Melee: Shock is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of inflicting the Shock Debuff when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.SHOCK.
Melee: Recover HP is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that gives a chance of restoring HP when auto-attacking with melee weapons. The Skell equivalent is M-Auto.HP-RECOVERY.

Mega Tensifiers are Consumable Items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be received as Division Rewards for Division activities. They can be used in battle to raise the Tension of all party members by 3,000 TP.
Melee Draw Surge is a ground weapon Soul Voice augment in and . It increases the chance of triggering the Draw Melee Soul Voice by 10% to 50%.
Meg is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.
Medium Wear is a type of Armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This class of armor has higher defense than Light Wear, with a penalty to Gravity Resistance and often fewer upgrades.
The Masterstroke Glaive is a craftable Longsword in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0101SS.
The Masterstroke Edges II are craftable Dual Swords in Xenoblade Chronicles X. These weapons can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0203SS.

Max TP Down is a debuff in . It reduces the maximum TP that a party member can have, which can restrict them from using TP arts or using Overdrive for a duration. It decreases max TP by 1000 at tier I, and by 500 extra for each tier above, except for tier VI which reduces TP by 4000.
Melee Accuracy Down is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It reduces melee attack accuracy.
Melee Accuracy is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It consists of the chance of landing a hit when using a melee attack.
Masterstroke Raidrifle is a ranged weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is an Assault Rifle and this weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-R0102SS.
The Masterstroke Glaive II is a craftable Longsword in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0102SS.
The Masterstroke Lance is a craftable Javelin in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0503SS.
The Masterstroke Sidearm are craftable Dual Guns in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-R0205SS.
The Masterstroke Deadsight is a craftable Sniper Rifle in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-R0503SS.
The Masterstroke Deadsight II is a craftable Sniper Rifle in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-R0504SS.
The Masterstroke Edges are craftable Dual Swords in Xenoblade Chronicles X. These weapons can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0204SS.
The Masterstroke Lightblade is a craftable Photon Saber in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0601SS.

Materials are a type of item in and . Materials are most often obtained by defeating enemies, and often take the form of a body part or possession of the defeated foe. Many materials can also be obtained by trading with NPCs, and a few are only available by trading. Like Key Items, some materials are required to complete Quests. The Quest Items include materials and key items which are needed for quest completion. After a certain point in the game, the Monado will sometimes show a vision when a material is collected. These materials will be needed for future quests, and are marked with a white exclamation mark on their icon. It is possible to trigger a vision for an item needed in a mutually
The Masterstroke Lightblade II is a craftable Photon Saber in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This weapon can be crafted at the AM Terminal after obtaining the Schematic FILE-M0602SS.

Merc Groups (Japanese: , Yōheidan) are a mechanic in . They consist of dispatching mercenary groups of Blades on timed tasks called Merc Missions (Japanese: , Yōheidan Ninmu). After some in-game time passes, the missions are completed in the background and the Blades return with a certain amount of Gold, EXP, Merc Points and treasure containing useful items. Sending Merc Groups to missions allows a Driver to improve the Affinity Chart of participating Blades and obtain Key Affinity Rewards that unlock new skill levels. Up to six Blades can join a squad for a mission, and up to three of these can be dispatched at once depending on the current Mercenary Level. Each team dispatched on a mission

Max (Japanese: , Makushimu) is an NPC in . Max is an Ardainian who can be found at Argentum Bazaar in the Argentum Trade Guild's Goldmouth. He runs a Courier service, which Rex can use to send money to his aunt Corinne. Rex must interact with him to send money to Corinne during the Story Quest Big Job Preparations. Rex interacts with Max again during Time is Money.

Melolo (Japanese: , Meroro) is an NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found at Central Exchange in the Argentum Trade Guild's Goldmouth. Melolo runs a shop called Central Exchange. She has a son named Bipopo who is involved in the DLC quest Nopon of Good Tastes, where their relationship is mentioned. Melolo gives no quests or Merc Missions, but she must be visited during Big Job Preparations.
The Megalo Aligo (Japanese: , Megaroejji Diburo) is a Boss in . It is a member of the Aligo family that is fought at level 4 in the Engine Room of the Ancient Ship.

Martial Kamron (Japanese: , Kihei no Īnasu) is a Unique Monster in . He is a Driver fought alongside his Blade at level 23 at the Stone Gate Ruins in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya. He must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 2 Adamantine Axe Blade Special.

Menes Drivers (Japanese: , Menebu Doraibā) are enemies in . They are Drivers fought alongside their Blades. One can found at level 21 at the Stone Gate Ruins in the Kingdom of Uraya, alongside a Gottarm Driver and the Martial Kamron.
Massive Mushroom Pies are Staple Food Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Rumbletum Canteen in Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Boreas.

Martz Parisax (Japanese: , Mūzu Parasu) are enemies in . They are members of the Parisax family, and can be found at level 30-34 in the Dragon's Stomach in of Kingdom of Uraya, while level 59-61 ones spawn from Breed Eggs.

Masrah Spring (Japanese: , Masura no Izumi) is a location in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Gormott Province just beyond Old Ghostwood Road and leading up to Outlook Knoll. There are two Treasure Troves here. Visiting this location with Elma, Tora, Nia, Mòrag, and Zeke in the party is necessary to unlock Elma's level 1 "Keen Eye" Field Skill.

Melnath's Shoulder (Japanese: , Merunasu Hidarikata-ku) is a location in . It is located on the left side of the upper level of the Gormott Province and is the massive slope between the Greatspine Boundary and Umon's Shipyard. The Sealstone of Earth can be found here.
The Mercenary HQ (Japanese: , Yatoi Heidan Honbu) is a Landmark in . It is located in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya, next to Harghalgh Inn.
The Memorial Ruins (Japanese: , Seisen Atochi) are a landmark in . They are located in the Head of Tantal, between the Great Pillar Passage and Genbu Crown.

Merclibay Islet (Japanese: , Merukuribe Kojima) is a location in . It is located in the Rigitte Waters in the Leftherian Archipelago, south of the Little Garden of Tradition, and below Baldotas Isle. There is a Treasure Trove here, and an air flow that launches the party back up to Baldotas Isle. There are no enemies here except during Merclibay's Mightiest.

The Megaflote Base (Japanese: , Megafurōto Kibu) is a landmark in . It is located at the base of the World Tree in the Land of Morytha, above the World Tree Root. It contains a lift to Benetnash, Elevator #6. There are no enemies here, but Mikhail can be recruited as a Blade here during New Game Plus after Indol sinks during Chapter 9. The in-game location and the map are mislabeled: the World Tree is listed on the map as a location where the Megaflote Base should be, and the Megaflote Base is listed as a landmark where the World Tree should be.
The Megrez Gateway (Japanese: , Gēto Obu Zeburu) is a landmark in . It is located on the Upper Level of the World Tree, between Alioth, Elevator #3 and Lv. 4, Megrez. There are no enemies here.

Megrez, Elevator #1 (Japanese: , Zeburu Dai-1 Erebētā) is a location in . It is located on the Upper Level of the World Tree, beyond Lv. 4, Megrez and leads up to the Rhadamanthus Portal. There are no enemies here.
Melodious Melon Parfaits are Dessert Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Honeycomb Sweets in Goldmouth of the Argentum Trade Guild. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Poppi QTπ.
Meat & Lentil Skewers are Meat Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Bassani Butchers in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Master's Curries are Staple Food Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Brad Flatforms in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of KOS-MOS and both forms of MOMO.
Masterpieces of Alrest are Literature Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Aldomar Books in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Memoria Art is a shop in . It is run by Tephloneo and can be found at night in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. It specializes in Art.
Meatball Pots-au-Feu are Meat Pouch items in . They can be created by Pyra at the kitchens in Tora's House and Corinne's House. Two are needed for Crossette's level 2 Fortitude Field Skill.

Mees Urchons (Japanese: , Misōru Unin) are enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family and can be found at level 4 at Goldmouth Exit Dock and the Salvage Deck at the Argentum Trade Guild during rainy weather. This enemy drops no items.
Mayne Drivers (Japanese: , Meine Doraibā) are enemies in . They are Drivers. One can be found at level 8 at Torigoth Market in Torigoth, Gormott Province, standing in front of the Notice Board.

Meldl Skwarors (Japanese: , Merudo Sutora) are enemies in . They are members of the Skwaror family and can be found at level 25-27 on the Upper Level - Right of the Gormott Province, particularly near Boulderbore Gate, near Honeypot Grotto, or around the wooden house near Lyta Oasis. Four must be defeated in order to unlock T-elos's level 2 "Heaven's Tracker" on her affinity chart.

|-|XC2 = |-|TTGC = Melosian Honey are Flower collectibles in and . They can be collected from several Collection Points located in Honeypot Grotto in the Gormott Province. In they are found in large amounts in the flower patches north of the Hoary Weald Camp.

Massido Arduns (Japanese: , Musaido Arudon) are enemies in . They are members of the Ardun family and can be found at level 17-25 in the Kingdom of Uraya, particularly at Sternum Arch, on the Cobalt Cliffs, at Drillbore Bridge or on Funnystone Highway. They are level 17-21 in the Head and 21-25 in the Stomach. Two must be defeated to unlock Corvin's level 2 Ex Tenebris Lux Blade Special.

Maxello is an NPC in . He is an Indoline who can be found at Goetius Port in the Indoline Praetorium. Maxello runs a shop called Cafe Lutino specialized in Drinks. He later moves to Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago after Chapter 8.
The Memoria Deeds are a Store Deed key item in . They can be purchased from Memoria Art in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.

Matchul Tirkin (Japanese: , Macheru Tākin) are quest-exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 38 at the Tirkin Turf in the Gormott Province during the quest Our Daily Bread.
Melz Runners (Japanese: , Meruse Rannā) are enemies in . They are members of the Skwaror family, and can be found at level 21-27 at Minnet Terrace or the Stone Gate Ruins in the Kingdom of Uraya.

Mayn Elucas (Japanese: , Maiyan Erūka) are enemies in . They are members of the Eluca family, and can be found at level 32-34 around Daram Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Brighid's level 2 Swirling Dragon, Newt's level 3 Immolating Cleave, Dagas's level 3 Tyrant Crush, and Praxis's level 2 Foam Blast on their affinity charts.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Mechanized Greaves (Japanese: , Kikaika Regāsu) are accessories in and . They increase damage dealt against toppled enemies by up to 60%. The Crystal Greaves, Graphite Greaves and Staunch Boots accessories offer stronger instances of this equipment's effect.

Memory Lockets (Japanese: , Omoide no Roketto) are accessories in and . They prevent the wearer from losing Affinity when they are incapacitated, allowing them to keep the current level of the Affinity Bond upon getting revived.
Mechanical Branches are Tree collectibles in . They can be found on the World Tree.
Melancholy Leaves are Tree collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Tantal. In the , Melancholy Leaves can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Melancholy Roses are Flower collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Tantal. In the , Melancholy Roses can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Masnach Exchange is a shop in . It is run by Llin and can be found at Torigoth Market in the Gormott Province. It specializes in Exchanging.
Martietta Trading is a shop in . It can be found in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. It is specialized in Exchange.
Mega Muscle (Japanese: , Birudomassuru, Lit. "Build Muscle") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Vandham's arts when using the Dual Scythes.
Masqued Devils are Treasure items in . They can be obtained through Salvaging in the Leftherian Archipelago, particularly at Rigitte Harbor and at Fonsett Village's Messet Point.
Memory Devices Gb-64 are Treasure items in . They can be obtained through Salvaging at 7th Perimeter Skyport on the World Tree.
Maryn is an NPC in . Maryn is an Urayan who can be found in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. Maryn gives the quest Family vs. Fiends.
Marvelous Mercenaries is a Quest in . It can be received from Yew at Mercenary HQ in the Kingdom of Uraya. After this quest finishes, the Merc Group will be raised to level 5.
Mason is an NPC in . He is a Leftherian carpenter who can be found at the Verde Carpentry Workshop in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Martal is an NPC in . He is a Tantalese who can be found in the area around Lake Varna in the Kingdom of Uraya during Eternal Spirit, where he is attacked by a Tronk Aligo. After being saved by the party, they bring him back to his mother Sornathea in Theosoir.
Menacing Jo (Japanese: , Odoshi no Jō) is a Driver Boss in . He is fought at level 25 alongside Benjamin the Brain and Cartbreaker Grzeg in the Brigands' Hideout in the Gormott Province.
Marshy is an NPC in . Marshy is an Urayan who can be found near Brad Flatforms in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Menda is an NPC in . Menda is an Urayan who can be found at the small dock by the Commercial District in the Kingdom of Uraya.

The Masterpiece Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Bumper Crop. It enables the purchase of Masterpieces of Alrest from the Aldomar Books shop at Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya.

Meet and Greet is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Soul reaches Level 9. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Wind Mastery" and "Ice Mastery" Field Skills. It increases Ursula's fanbase by a large amount. This mission will become unobtainable if not unlocked before the end of the quest.

Medicine Knowledge is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain from Smaia during A Secret Cure, and must be completed as part of that quest. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Focus", "Water Mastery" and "Nopon Wisdom" Field Skills.

Materials Stakeout is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the Main Story Quest Lila's Location, upon reaching the entrance to the Old Industrial District. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Fortitude", "Info Collector" and "Expeditionist" Field Skills. This Merc Mission is only available during Lila's Location. It will disappear from the menu if the alternate objective is completed and the Barrels' Destination info item is obtained.
This quest is missable and will expire during Chapter 8. Mellica the Chorister is a quest in . It can be received from Mellica at Seoris Plaza in the Indoline Praetorium.
Mellica is an NPC in . She is a young Gormotti who can be found at Seoris Plaza in the Indoline Praetorium. She gives the quest Mellica the Chorister.
Merciless Twister is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when using a Cobra Bardiche. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0).

Mastery of Sky Sparks (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Brilliant Twinblades. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Mòrag's Revolution Flash.
Matharie is an NPC in . She is a Urayan who can be found in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya. She runs an Informant shop specialized in information.

Menacing Lariat (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Sword Tonfa. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Zeke's Hammer Lariat.

Mercenary Points or Merc Points, commonly referred to as MP, are a game mechanic in . They can be earned by completing Merc Group Missions and can be used to level up the Merc Group. When enough Merc Points are obtained, the Merc Group is able to level up, by heading to the Mercenary HQ in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya. There, Yew or Zuo will confront the party with a Quest needing to be complete in order to level up the Merc Group.

Meddlesome Zacharias (Japanese: , Sewayaki Zakusu) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . He is a Driver enemy who can be found at level 60 at the Balquors Ruins on the Cliffs of Morytha alongside Profligate Sjell during Upgrades and Tinkering. Although it is not specifically required to defeat these enemies to complete the quest, they serve as obstacles to one of its objectives and must be fought or otherwise evaded to continue onwards. Upon completing said objective, both enemies will permanently despawn.
Maximum Affinity is an Info Item in . It can be purchased from the Informant shop at the Market of Torigoth in the Gormott Province.
Merc Rewards 1 are an Info Item in . It can be purchased from the Informant shop at the Kedeigh Gate of Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Merc Rewards 2 are an Info Item in . It can be purchased from the Informant shop at the Kedeigh Gate of Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Max Affinity is an Info Item in . It can be purchased from Darryth, the Informant in Fonsa Myma, for a base price of 800 G.
The Merc Mission Tip is an Info Item in . It can be purchased from Matharie, the Informant in Garfont Village, Uraya, for a base price of 1,100 G.

Masque Scouts (Japanese: , Masuke Sukauto) are Story Exclusive Enemies in . They are Ardainian Soldiers that can be found at level 23-27 throughout Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain during Chapter 4.
Mattragh is an NPC in . He can be found in the Torigoth Relay Base in the Gormott Province, where he trains recruits. He must be spoken to in order to trigger the Blade Quest Newt Recruits.

Merclibay's Mightiest is a DLC Quest in . It is part of the New Quests Pack 3 of the Expansion Pass. It can be accepted during Chapter 10 by speaking to Caephon at Rigitte Harbor in the Leftherian Archipelago with Electra, Zenobia, and Herald in the party. Electra's Mastery of Thunder Lv 5 and Herald's Rampage Lv 5 field skills are required to receive the quest.

Matteo is an NPC in . He is an Urayan who can be found at the Royal Guard Barracks in the Kingdom of Uraya during the DLC Quest A Mercenary's Honor available as downloadable content, the New Quests Pack 3 of the Expansion Pass.

The Megayogre Aligo (Japanese: , Megayogore Diburo) is a Challenge Battle Enemy in . It is a member of the Aligo family that is fought at level 63 during the fourth wave of the Challenge Battle Panic at the Seaside.

The Megaspoony Aligo (Japanese: , Megasupūnī Diburo) is a Challenge Battle Enemy in . It is a member of the Aligo family that is fought at level 66 during the final wave of the Challenge Battle Panic at the Seaside. This enemy drops no items.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Master Scopes (Japanese: , Masutāgurasu) are DLC accessories in and . They reduce an enemy's resistance to Break inflicting Arts used by the wearer. They are the upgraded version of the Beta Scope accessory. They can be found in the Land of Challenge from Treasure Troves obtained after completing a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass.
The Marsanes is a vehicle in . It is the warship and base of Torna.

The Median Gate (Japanese: , Mediumu-mon, Medium Gate) is a landmark in . It is located in the center of Auresco, and serves as the main entryway to the Sachsum Gardens and Aureus Palace from Pischator Bridge.
Mechanical Charms are Charms in . They can be created by Lora at Campsites.
Marrin Fishmeats are Enemy Part collectible items in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Torna. They can be dropped by Legarre Marrins.
Memento Barks are Tree collectible items in . They can be found in Gormott. Alongside Sticky Stick Insects, they are required for every Script Minoth can make with Dramaturgy.

Mauna is an NPC in . She is an elderly Tornan shopkeeper who can be found near the Formide Shopping Ward in the Kingdom of Torna. Mauna offers no quests, but her Community is gained upon speaking to her after completion of A Rare Sense of Justice.

Marrith Antols (Japanese: , Marisu Antoru) are quest exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, and can be found at level 38 in the Kingdom of Torna during the quest Homegrown Inventor. As with all quest exclusive enemies in , they drop no items, only gold.
Melille is an NPC in . She is a Leftherian who is found in the Fonsett Residential Area of the Leftherian Archipelago.

Maulton is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian chef who can be found near Auresco, Main Gate in the Kingdom of Torna, at Sorrel's café. He is involved in the quest Great Tornan Cook-Off, and his Community is gained alongside Sorrel's upon its completion.
Melekanze is a Machina NPC in . She can be found at the Old Expedition HQ on the Bionis' Shoulder after the Teelan's Laboratory attack event, whereupon she gives the quest Shoulder Survey Snaps.
Merciful Heart (Japanese: , Māshifuruhāto) is Nia's Level II Blade Special in .
Melancholic Break (Japanese: Merankorībureikā, Lit. "Melancholy Breaker") is Kasandra's Level IV Blade Special in .
Martial Artistry is a light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. It can be found inside a Giants' Trove at Agni's Skygarden Ruins.
Mega Spinning Edge (Japanese: , Megasupin'ejji, Lit. "Mega Spin Edge") is Noah's Ouroboros Talent Art in .
Medic Gunner (Japanese: , Medikkugan'nā) is a Kevesi Healer class in .
Menno Arch (Japanese: , Meno no Daidōmon) is a Landmark in , located in the Eagus Wilderness.
Martial Artist (Japanese: , Māsharuātisuto) is an Agnian Attacker class in and .
Melnath's Pass, Lower (Japanese: , Merunasu Yamamichi Kasō) is a Location in . It is located on Melnath's Shoulder in the Aetia Region.
The Material Storage Warehouse (Japanese: , Busshi Hokanko) is a Landmark in . It is located at the Great Sword's Hilt.

Massive Georges (Japanese: , Kyototsu no Jarusha) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 37 in the Hidden Freshwater Inlet at Great Cotte Falls. The Fin of Fear Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
Mehnert Interdigit (Japanese: , Menāto no Shikan) is a Location in . It is located north of Colony Iota on Elaice Highway.
Matryos Carbons are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
The Memorial Ropl is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Ropl family, and is fought at level 62 on Melnath's Pass, Lower on Melnath's Shoulder during My Memories.
Menaas Aspars are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Aspar family, and can be found at level 32-33 in High Maktha Wildwood in the Pentelas Region.

Max Effort is a Battle Art in . It is one of Fiona's arts as a Hero, and is a variant of Aureole used by Ouroboros.

Melekanze's Camera is a Key Item in . It is a camera owned by Melekanze that she lends to the party to take photos of a Glow Deinos and a Dozy Eluca during Shoulder Survey Snaps.

Megiddo King Quos are enemies in . They are Quo machines, and can be found in Volitaris.

Megiddo Puges are enemies in . They are Puge machines, and can be found in Volitaris.
Megiddo Eagle Galdrs are enemies in . They are Galdr machines, and can be found in Volitaris.
The Meaty Suid is a Mission Exclusive Secondary Boss in . It is a member of the Suid family, and can be found at level 55 near Sayram Lake in Primordia during One Big Happy Family.

Metal Face (, Kuroi Feisu, Black Face) is one of the antagonists in . He is the first Faced Mechon to be introduced. He is the main reason Shulk begins the journey to the Bionis' head and serves as the antagonist along with Xord throughout the first half of the game.
Mobile Artillery are heavily armed Vehicles in created by the Homs for defensive use against the Mechon.

Minana (Japanese: , Minka) is a Nopon in . She can be found at Kyn Shopping Street next to the Frontier Village Weapon Shop in Frontier Village. If she is invited to Colony 6, she can be found near the Nopon house next to the lake.

Merisa (Japanese: , Merissa, Melissa) is a High Entia in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found on the walkway far to the north of the Imperial Palace in Alcamoth, nearby the rest station from about 06:00 to 18:00. When approaching from the south she can be a bit hard to spot because she is right behind a small raised bed of vegetation, close to the fence. She is the mother of Mir'leiz.

Mir'leiz (Japanese: , Mirarīsu) is a High Entia in . He can be found in Alcamoth, southwest of the Imperial Palace. He is just before the entrance to the southern infinity-shaped bridge, next to a small fountain, from 06:00 to 18:00. Mir'leiz is the son of Merisa. During Bring Back My Son!, he can be found anytime at the Hovering Reef 1 in Eryth Sea.

Miller (Japanese: , Mirā) is a Homs in . He can be found in the northern portion of the Commercial District or the Military District in Colony 9. Emmy Leater claims he runs so fast he can get away from her in three seconds flat.
Minnie (Japanese: , Meinī) is a Homs in . She can be found in the southwestern portion of the Residential District of Colony 9.

Migaga (Japanese: , Migamiga) is a Nopon in . She can be found at the Sacred Altar in the middle of the Central Plaza of Frontier Village. She will appear once Chief Dunga leaves the altar, after completing the Story Quest An Errand for the Heropon.

Modamo (Japanese: , Modanī) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found in the northeastern portion of the Archaeology Level in Frontier Village. When giving Lousy Lizards, he reveals that he trained Riki.
Miko (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in . She can be found in the Prophecy Hut in Frontier Village. Her house is located near the Contemplation Terrace at the Apex Lake.

Meyneth (Japanese: , Meinasu, Maynus; English dub: ), also referred to by her venerators as Lady Meyneth, is a supporting character in . She is the soul of Mechonis and Zanza's equal. She wields her own Monado in combat, and is addressed as Lady Meyneth by all Machina. Bionis life simply call her Meyneth.

Modern Blue Gears (Japanese: , Modan Burū Gia) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they are efficiently-constructed gearwheels so beautiful that it is a shame to use them.

Minute Mantises (Japanese: , Nanajuunanafushi) are collectables in . They are part of the Other page of the Collectopaedia, and can only be acquired by trading with Sonia in Colony 9. According to their description, they are giant bugs with 77 stripes and they never move, making them hard to find. Obtaining one will unlock the "Mysterious Mantis" achievement.

Mining is an important mechanic in and . Crystals can be mined from Ether Crystal deposits, as shown in the picture to the right. The first crystal deposit is in Tephra Cave, near the Spring of Grief. The Ether Mine has the most places to mine crystals. Some deposits have more than one spot where crystals can be collected. Others have one mining deposit but will allow crystals to be collected a few times. Small deposits which have been exhausted will take five minutes to replenish while big deposits take ten minutes. The time only counts down while being in the actual game and not in menus. In , gems are not crafted but mined directly from the high-quality Ether deposits on Bionis' Shoulder.

Mixik (Japanese: , Minisu) is a young Machina in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found from 21:00 to 03:00 in the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm, in front of the entrance to Junks. She is the daughter of Kazat and Qofaria.

Miriall (Japanese: , Miria) is a High Entia in . She can be found southwest of the Imperial Palace in Alcamoth, next to the fountain from 18:00 to 06:00. After the events at the Mechonis Core, she relocates to the Ether Plant in Eryth Sea. She can be found on the main platform of the Ether Plant from 18:00 to 06:00.

Mining Patrichev (Japanese: , Saikutsu no Patorichefu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of the earliest monsters seen in Tephra Cave. It is a level 8 Bunniv, and can be found northeast of the Caterpile Nest in an indentation in the wall. It drops Heavy Bunniv Iron, two pieces of which are needed to complete the quest Education-Crazy Suzanna.

Mist Rhoguls (Japanese: , Misuto Rōguru) are enemies in . They are members of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 25 in Satorl Marsh during the day, west of the Nopon Refuge, near the Altar of Fate, and near the Statue Summit. Defeating two of them is required to complete the Satorl Marsh's quest Monster Quest 3. They can drop the Rhogul Axe Crests needed for Bridge Repair.

Merry Coronations (Japanese: , Merī Kangiku) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Satorl Marsh and Colony 6. According to their description, they sway joyfully even when there is no wind and they are perfect ornamental plants.

Mist Trees (Japanese: , Kiri no Kiri, Empress Tree of Mist) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, they are a form of timber unique to the area and they need to be sanded to be used.

A Metal Lancer (Japanese: , Metaruransā) is a Weapon in . It is one of Reyn's gunlances. It can be purchased in Colony 9 and is dropped by a large variety of enemies around Colony 9 and in Tephra Cave.

Million Drivers (Japanese: , Mirionbankā) are weapons in . They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can be obtained from various low-level enemies in Colony 9 and Tephra Cave. Million Drivers can also be obtained through trade.

Missing Trees (Japanese: , Misshingu Tsurī) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they are soft trees that never decay when they go through genetic manipulation.

Mist Gel (Japanese: , Misuto Jeru) is light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is part of the swimsuit-style Mist Set along with the Mist Oil, Mist Cream, Mist Trunks, and Mist Sandals. It is dropped by several enemies in Satorl Marsh and can be received as rewards from Preventing Starvation and Disinsectization.

The Military District (Japanese: , Gunji-ku) is a location in . It is one of the three districts of Colony 9, and the base of the Colony 9 Defence Force. Shulk's Weapon Development Lab is located here. At the entrance to the Military District is the Fortress Entrance.

Missing Lodger (Japanese: , Yukuefumei no Dōkyonin) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Ma'crish in Reconstruction HQ in Colony 6. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment. After completing this quest, Nopo'rikh may offer Looking for Freedom.
The Middle Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Reyn's initial arm armour and are not otherwise available.

Middle Gear (Japanese: , Midoru Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is part of the Middle Set along with the Middle Armour, Middle Gauntlets, Middle Leggings, and Middle Boots. It is part of Reyn's initial equipment and is not available elsewhere. Although classified as medium armour, it has the same icon as most of the light head armours, including Colony Cap and Nine Cap.
Middle Armour is medium torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is Reyn's initial torso armour and is not otherwise available.
Middle Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Reyn's initial legs armour and are otherwise unavailable.
Middle Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Reyn's initial feet armour and are otherwise unavailable.
Mist Trunks are light legs armour in . They can be dropped by Aqua Nebulae in Satorl Marsh.
Mist Cream is light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as quest rewards and from defeating various enemies in Satorl Marsh.
Mithril Gear (Japanese: , Misuriru Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is made with mithril ore from the Hovering Reefs in Eryth Sea.
Mithril Armour is medium torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is made from mithril ore from the Hovering Reefs.
Mithril Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made with mithril ore from one of the Hovering Reefs of Eryth Sea.
Messenger Shoes are medium feet armour in . They are worn by messengers in the Homs army. They can be dropped by various Bunnits.
Mithril Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made with mithril ore from one of the Hovering Reefs in Eryth Sea.

The Meyneth Statue (Japanese: , Kubinashi Meinasu-zō) is a landmark in . It is a statue of Meyneth, the goddess of Mechonis, and is located in Zedonia Plaza, on floor 2F of Agniratha. The statue is roughly 2½ times taller than a Homs and is missing its head. Four collectable orbs appear at night on or around the statue. The Wise Gremory, a Unique Monster, can be found on a bridge directly west of the landmark.
Mithril Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made with mithril ore from one of the Hovering Reefs in Eryth Sea.
Meteor Nibbler (Japanese: , Ryūseigun no Bakubaku, Meteor Shower Nibbler) is a weapon in . It is a Biter wielded by Riki, and is the Biter with the highest attack.

The Message in a Bottle is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is required for Liliana's Sincere Request. It is located at the northeast most part of the map (the northern tip of the Agora Shore), and guarded by a Unique Monster - the Gentle Rodriguez. However, it is possible to get the item by luring it out then running and sneaking behind its back.
Mirage Staves (Japanese: , Mirājusutaffu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staves that can be wielded by Melia.
The Mini Reactor is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is dropped by the Experimental M86, and is needed for The Mini Reactor.

Meteor Staves (Japanese: , Mītiasutaffu) are weapons in and . They are staves that can be wielded by Melia. Among all of her staves with three empty slots, they have the highest maximum attack value. __TOC__
Mist Oil is light torso armour in . It can be dropped by various enemies.

Mischievious Naberius (Japanese: , Akugi no Naberiusu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a level 57 Fortress-type Mechon found behind 3rd Gate in Sword Valley. It is by far the strongest Unique Monster in Sword Valley.

Mind Blast (Japanese: , Maindoburasuto) is one of Melia's Ether arts in and . It can only be used when Melia is in Element Burst mode. It targets enemies in a broad area ahead of Melia. It can inflict Arts Seal and remove any auras from the enemies it hits.

The Mist Radiant is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of the four radiants that must be collected for Imperial Ceremony Offerings, and can only be obtained while this quest is active. It is located in the Basin Cave in Satorl Marsh.

The Misty Path (Japanese: , Kiri no Kaidō) is a landmark in . It is the road that leads from Colony 6 to Satorl Marsh. It is located far south from the Pod Depot. At its northernmost area, it is inhabited by Colony Wisps at night and Clima Fliers in the day. During Chapter 17, two Polkan Telethia are also present here.

Mild Florence (Japanese: , Dantō no Furorensu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found in the Central Factory up a ramp near Landing Strip 2.

The Mobile Furnace is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received upon completion of The Gem Man's Invention. The Mobile Furnace allows the party to craft gems anywhere, instead of only at the Gem Man's Stall.

The Meyneth Cloister is a location in . It is located on the third floor of Agniratha. Ending with the Meyneth Shrine, Meyneth Cloister is a balcony directly underneath the giant effigy of Lady Meyneth. The Meyneth Shrine is where the party fights Egil for the first time.

The Meyneth Shrine (Japanese: , Meinasu Shinden) is a landmark in . It is located on the third floor of Agniratha, at the end of the Meyneth Cloister. As the name suggests, it is a shrine dedicated to Meyneth.

The Mining Base (Japanese: , Saikutsu Kichi) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine, branching off from the Storage Depot. It is a small room filled with controls and machines, a bed, and what looks like a shuttered viewing window. This is presumably where Otharon stayed after the Colony 6 Defence Force was overrun, and is also where Emmy Leater flees to during A Young Captain's Trust. A Heart-to-Heart - "A Broken Watch" - between Shulk and Sharla can be accessed here.
The Middle Housing Level (Japanese: , Chūsō Jūtaku-ban) is a location in . It is located on the third floor of Frontier Village.
Millesaurs (Japanese: , Mirezauro) are enormous, dinosaur-like creatures in .
Missions are a game mechanic in . Similar to quests in , missions are an easy and efficient way for the party to gain EXP, BP, credits, and items such as armor and weapons.

Miriall's Telescope is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Miriall during Starlight Seeker, and must be delivered to Elior to complete the quest. It can be received a second time from Elior during Starlight Gazer when he asks the party to find someone who can improve it.

Mining Probes are types of Data Probes in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They improve productivity from a FrontierNav Site, increasing the amount of obtainable Miranium and allowing valuable resources to be extracted. The higher the probe's level, the greater the amount of Miranium obtained and the quantity of resources extracted. If mining probes of the same grade are linked they will be more effective. For example three mining G2 probes linked together will give an 30% increase but 1 x G1 and 2 x G2 mining probes will not. The Model Viewer is a special feature in the Collection Mode exclusive to (along with the Jukebox), whereby the player can view and interact with character models from the game. In the beginning, there are only a few models available, but as the player progresses through the story, more become available over the course of the game. Models are unlocked using tokens earned from the Model Raffle in Collection mode, and tokens can be earned in three ways: 3 for scanning the Shulk amiibo, 2 for every hit in StreetPass, and 1 for every 5 Play Coins earned.
